questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. You can pretty much google your way to an affordable apartment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Don't live close to the school, live downtown, that's where the pulse of the city is.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, although it did take a while to fill out the different application forms etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The student coordinator was very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: To be honest it was pretty difficult. The classes are almost randomly spread out throughout the semester, so there is really no coherent structure in it. But you will just need to adapt, and get the most of it.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take the classes that sounds the most strange. For instance, I had a class called introduction to Islamic legal Thought which was very interesting. A class in that category would never be taught in Denmark. So take everything that sounds almost weird to you. Especially if you are a law student and are used to just going through paragraphs and paraphrasing old professors.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses vary a lot in their levels. Overall I want to say that the amount of reading and preparation for each class is A LOT lower than at the University of Copenhagen. However, that english level at which many of the classes are taught are pretty high, and if you are willing to engage in the discussions you will find that the level is quite a lot higher than one might expect.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Well I went to UCPH during covid, so some of the classes were online. However the biggest difference was the preparation for each class was much less at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Federalism and the European Union. International Law of the Sea. Human Rights. Introduction to Islamic Legal Thought. Introduction to Law in a digital Economy. Law in the age of climate change. EU Energy and Environmental Law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to Islamic Legal Thought. Very interesting and different course. Should definitely be taught in more countries as far as I'm concerned.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I regret not going on more trips perhaps. So do just about everything you can.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Porto.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Have an open mind. You didn't travel all the way for nothing, so go meet new people and strike up a conversation with someone whom you perhaps never would've talked to on your home country.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Outgoing party vibe

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Mingle with the other students, not just the ones from your country, or the Erasmus program in general. 2. Eat everything strange that you can get your hands on. 3. Don't get lost in Bairro Alto when you are drunk. That place is a maze.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy and have fun with it. School is only so much of the experience.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: weather, food, drinks, friends, the charme of the city

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That I didn't have more time

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
